items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: I see a friend of mine from Gene Krupa's band. By name of [Murphy DeFono]

ctx.x: had sounded too good, they would have taken over. So at the end of the dance, the band valet, his name was Mutt, came back and said, "John, you and Sid. There's a soldier out here that wants to see you all. Say you are the only two in the band he know." I say, "Yeah," well, I was dressed, I'd changed. Sid was still standing there, soaking wet. He was trying to dry off, cool off and everything.

I said, "Sid, I'm going to go across the street and get some cigarettes and Pepsi, and I'll see who it is." And I get outside the dressing room, and I see a friend of mine from Gene Krupa's band. By name of [Murphy DeFono] He had a jet black hair with a lock hanging up front, you know, nice looking guy. Trumpet player. Now,he hadn't had any Army training, boot training at all. He was in the band. Here comes this Macon, Georgia policeman, with his jeans on, his cowboy boots, and his hog leg hanging down -- hog…

billy clubs. "You Yankee son of a bitch. Didn't we tell you not to speak to no niggers down here?" "But they're friends of mine." Whop, whop, whop. He was adding to the injury, you know. And they almost killed him.
